children: Life360's bull at Citi thinks the location-app developer's annual earnings guidance still looks conservative. Dual-listed Life360 narrowed its adjusted Ebitda guidance range to US$132 million-US$138 million from US$130 million-US$140 million, but analyst Siraj Ahmed thinks the unchanged US$135 million range midpoint could be too low given the company's improved expectations for higher-margin subscription revenue. Overall, Ahmed tells clients in a note that Life360's third-quarter result was positive. Citi has a last-published buy rating and US$60.00 target price on Life360's U.S.-listed stock. Its Australia-listed shares are down 8.9% at A$20.35. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)
